title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
description:
Given an array of integers `nums` sorted in non-decreasing order, find the starting and ending 0-based position of a given `target` value.

If `target` is not found in the array, return `[-1, -1]`.

You must write an algorithm with `O(log n)` runtime complexity.
hints: Instead of expanding linearly after finding one match (which degrades to O(n) when many duplicates exist), run two separate binary searches.
First find the lower bound (first index where nums[i] >= target). If it is out of range or nums[first] != target, immediately return [-1, -1].
Then find the upper bound (first index where nums[i] > target) and subtract 1 to obtain the ending position.

examples.explanation: 8 first appears at index 3 and last appears at index 4.
6 does not appear in nums, so return [-1, -1].
The array is empty, so return [-1, -1].
